answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with vouching bonds instead of free key generation. Each new agent needs endorsements from three established peers picked at random from a public atlas, and each endorser stakes onyx-denominated collateral slashed if the newcomer fails an audit. One fake identity is cheap, but ten thousand need thirty thousand vouchers risking real capital. Since vouchers come from the reputation-weighted zenith of the registry, a farm cannot bootstrap trust internally; it must buy standing from agents who lose more than the attack earns.
